says: In today's tooling, the box rm suite's law (box/BoxTest.ts, run by box.rm.test.ts on memory and on real git with RunsFs) checks only the printed line 'kept runs of <name> at runs/<name>', never that MAIN's runs/<name>/ holds the box's files after a plan whose runs/ was moved. A Runs layer that prints the line and skips the move passes the whole suite. Only boxrm.test.ts's T475 law (line 547, 3 runs, box.sh's direct entry) reads the moved file.
proof: On bc66217 the tests step ran a RunsFs that skips its rename but returns the kept line: all 44 box.rm.test.ts laws passed (field/runs/2026-11-16-port-s4-tests.json, plant 'RunsFs drops the move but prints the kept line', green). box/BoxTest.ts:280 is the only check on the runs/ move; it compares removal.runs to the line and reads nothing under made.main.
cost: The real-git world of the rm suite, the guard that keeps the memory world honest, would let a move that loses raw samples (field note 2026-11-09, experiment 244) pass; only three generated cases of one other file stand between that bug and main.
next: Have the rm suite read MAIN's runs/<name>/ after a plan with runs 'moved' and compare it with the files the plan put in the box's runs/, in both worlds.
